findings.description: The chore/refactor, docs and spike headings in the code don't match the labels in the repo's issue forms. Every form-filed chore, refactor, docs or spike ticket reports a required field as missing, and intake would strip `ready` from even a fully filled ticket.
findings.body:
GitHub issue forms render each field as `### <label>`. `sections()` matches headings exactly once `normalize()` has run, and `normalize()` never drops a word. Three headings in `REQUIRED_FIELDS` don't match the labels in the issue forms, the rubrics in `docs/tickets/`, or ADR 0176:

- **Chore/refactor:** `chore-refactor.yml`, `docs/tickets/chore-refactor.md` and ADR 0176 all say **"Proof that behavior is unchanged"**. The code has `'Proof behavior is unchanged'` (line 36).
- **Docs and spike:** they share one form, `docs-spike.yml`, whose first field is **"What changes, or the question"**. That label normalizes to `what changes or the question`. The code looks up `'What changes'` for docs (line 55) and `'Question'` for spike (line 57), and neither key exists in a form-rendered body.
- **Docs fields:** ADR 0176 gives docs/spike "what changes, or the question, the time box and the form of the answer". Docs tickets currently skip the Time box and Form of the answer checks.

**Trigger:** a correctly filled chore issue gets `missing: ['Proof behavior is unchanged']`. A docs issue gets `missing: ['What changes']` and a spike issue gets `missing: ['Question']`. Decision 176 says intake removes `ready` on a failed check.

**A second effect for docs:** `What changes` is that type's only area field, so `areaText` is empty. A docs ticket never fires the adr-area, module-boundary or `package.json` triggers.

The tests (lines 45, 50, 55-60) build their bodies from the code's own headings, not from the form labels, so they don't catch this.

**Fix:**
- Use the form labels verbatim.
- Give docs and spike the same three fields.
- Decide which docs field carries the paths. The form describes "Form of the answer" as the pages that will hold the change.

findings.description: A directory-style area such as `src/cli/ and src/core/` (the form-placeholder style) yields no module and no ADR match, so a bug or chore that crosses modules or touches an ADR area gets `needsDesign: false`.
findings.body:
The final segment of `PATH` needs at least one character, so `src/cli/ and src/core/` matches as `src/cli` and `src/core`, with no trailing slash. Both halves of the design check then miss.

**Module boundary.** `moduleOf('src/cli')` splits into `['src','cli']`. That fails `parts.length > 2`, so it returns `undefined`, `modules.size` is 0, and `module-boundary` never fires.

```ts
if (parts[0] === 'src' && parts.length > 2) return parts[1];
if (parts[0] === 'test' && parts.length > 3) return parts[2];
```

**ADR area.** `globToRegExp('src/cli/**')` gives `^src/cli/.*$`, which doesn't match `src/cli`. A `./src/cli/ls.ts` path also keeps its `./` on line 149: `moduleOf` strips it, but the ADR test does not, so that path misses as well.

**The forms invite directory answers:**
- `feature.yml`'s Affected area placeholder is `src/core/, \`pup plan\`, decision 40`.
- `bug.yml` asks for "the file, module or command you suspect".
- `chore-refactor.yml` asks for "One path or glob per line".

**Trigger:** a bug with `Suspected area: src/cli/ and src/core/` and `adrAreas: ['src/cli/**']` gets `triggers: []` and `needsDesign: false`. ADR 0176 forces a design on any type that "touches an ADR area, crosses a module boundary". Features are unaffected only because they need a design by default.

**Fix:**
- Strip a leading `./` from each path once, in `triggersFor`.
- Have `moduleOf` count a path without an extension as a directory.
- Test each ADR area against both `path` and `` `${path}/` ``.

findings.description: A `# comment` line inside a fenced code block is read as a heading and splits the section there. A shell comment in a reproduction or area block can make a filled field vague, or drop its paths so the design triggers don't fire.
findings.body:
`sections()` runs `HEADING.exec(line)` on every line and never tracks ```` ``` ```` or `~~~` fences. A shell comment such as `# fresh clone` matches `^#{1,6}\s+(.+?)…`, so everything after it moves into a new section that no check reads.

**Trigger A (a filled field reported vague):** `Reproduction` is ```` ```sh\n# fresh clone\npup ls\n``` ````. The field's value becomes ```` ```sh ````, one word in a non-terse field, so `isVague` returns true. `bug.yml` asks for "Exact steps from a clean state, with commands", so a fenced shell block is ordinary input there.

**Trigger B (the design gate wrongly passes):** `Suspected area` is ```` ```\n# from the stack trace\nsrc/core/a.ts\nsrc/cli/b.ts\n``` ````. The two paths land in a section called `from the stack trace`. `areaText` is then ```` ``` ````, so the result is `triggers: []` and `needsDesign: false`.

GitHub ignores headings inside fences, and an unclosed fence runs to the end of the document. The suggestion below gives the parser the same behaviour.

findings.description: `DesignTrigger` is a literal union in the exported return type. general.md requires "a `string` `enum` in the area's `enums/` folder, never a literal union" for a closed value set.

The exported `IntakeContext` interface is declared in a behavioural `*.utils.ts` file. general.md says "An exported or reused `type` / `interface` is never declared in a behavioural file". Move it to `src/core/types/`, or drop it (see the next nit).

`IntakeContext` is a one-field options object with one caller, which is the bloat general.md §Altitude names. Pass `adrAreas: string[]` directly and the interface and the `context.adrAreas` indirection both go away.

No issue form has an `Estimate` field, so the size trigger fires only when the author hand-writes an `### Estimate` heading. It then reads the first number in the section, so `2 slices, ~900 lines` reads as 2 and `1.5k lines` as 1, and neither fires the over-600 trigger.

The `PATH` doc says "a file name with an extension", but the regex only matches bare names ending in json, ts, js, md or yaml. A bare `foo.tsx` or `foo.py` in an area field never feeds the triggers. Name the extension set in the doc.
`ESTIMATE_HEADING` is used once, and that use wraps it in `normalize()`. Writing `sectionMap.get('estimate')` removes the constant, its doc comment and the extra call.
